target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(clawhub): reject mutable GitHub skill refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub marks GitHub-backed skill resolutions as immutable but OpenClaw trusted the resolver's `github.commit` string without enforcing a full commit SHA. A branch or tag such as `main` could therefore be downloaded, installed, and persisted as `mutable: false`, allowing the installed code to move behind an allegedly pinned identity.

This behavior is present in current `main`, stable `v2026.6.11`, and beta `v2026.7.1-beta.5`.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Validate the successful GitHub resolution once in `assertInstallResolutionAllowed`, before any download or filesystem side effect.
- Normalize the accepted commit to one trimmed, lowercase, 40-hex SHA in the returned resolution.
- Let version selection, GitHub codeload, install policy, origin metadata, lock metadata, and telemetry consume that same canonical object.
- Keep archive resolutions and direct `git:` installs unchanged; direct Git installs intentionally support mutable refs and record them as mutable.

The submitted later-stage validation was moved to the resolver acceptance boundary so downstream callers cannot accidentally reuse the raw ref.

## User Impact

Normal ClawHub GitHub-backed installs continue unchanged. A custom or malformed resolver response containing a branch, tag, short SHA, or other non-pinned ref now fails with clear guidance before download. This enforces ClawHub's documented 40-character commit contract; it adds no config, migration, or fallback surface.

## Evidence

- Existing pinned-install test now proves padded uppercase input is normalized and the canonical SHA reaches download, policy, origin, and installed version.
- New negative test proves `main` fails before archive download, extraction, policy evaluation, or installation.
- `oxfmt` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Autoreview: clean, 0.96 confidence.
- Official ClawHub protocol specifies a 40-character commit SHA; a live resolver sample returned a full SHA, while GitHub codeload accepts both a branch and SHA, proving client-side enforcement is necessary.
- Exact-head sanitized AWS focused tests passed 142 tests with two platform skips; `check:changed` passed.
- An actual CLI fixture returning mutable ref `main` failed before archive download or filesystem metadata.
- A live public ClawHub install carried resolver SHA `f6075a5060ed3c86536055700d95eb68655162ee` unchanged through codeload, origin, and lock metadata.
- Fresh hosted CI is rerunning on the unchanged final head after #104475 repaired an unrelated current-main guard assertion.

Root `CHANGELOG.md` is release-owned, so the release-note context and @yetval credit are carried here and in the replacement commit.

target.title: fix(firecrawl): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a Firecrawl `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the Firecrawl provider discards the execution context, so the request can remain open and eventually resolve after cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` / `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

The change does not alter Firecrawl configuration, schemas, caching, timeouts, SSRF policy, provider ordering, or response formatting. A focused test verifies the signal handoff.

Sibling PRs applying the same pattern: SearXNG (#104216 by zhangguiiping-xydt, 🐚 platinum hermit), Brave (#104269), plus the companion PRs filed alongside this one. The Google/Gemini provider already forwards the signal and serves as the reference.

## User Impact

Cancelling a run now promptly cancels an in-flight Firecrawl search instead of consuming network and server resources until the configured timeout or response. Normal completed searches and cached results are unchanged.

## Evidence

Focused suite passes on the rebased head, including the signal-forwarding test.

## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(agents): adopt orphaned managed worktrees left by a crash between git worktree add and registry insert
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A gateway crash (OOM kill, forced restart) landing between `git worktree add` and the registry insert inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves an on-disk worktree and an `openclaw/<name>` branch that no managed API can ever see, repair, or remove: `list()`/`get()` never show it, every `gc()` pass skips it forever, and any later `create()` with the same name fails hard with `branch already exists`. The only way out today is manual operator surgery (`git worktree remove` + `git branch -D`) outside the managed API. Reported with source-level analysis in #103239; this PR makes the orphan self-heal (gc adopts it; a retried create adopts it and preserves the caller's owner) while leaving foreign/detached worktrees untouched.

## Summary

- Problem: A crash between `git worktree add` and `insertRegistryWorktree()` inside `ManagedWorktreeService.create()` leaves a live git worktree + `openclaw/<name>` branch with no registry row. `reconcileOrphans()` explicitly skips it forever (invisible to `list()`/`gc()`), and a retried `create()` with the same name dead-ends on `branch already exists`.
- Why it matters: In real deployments (OOM kill, forced restart) the orphan is permanently unrecoverable through the managed API — only manual `git worktree remove` + `git branch -D` unblocks the name.
- What changed: recovery happens through the retried `create()` path only. `create()`'s branch-exists guard self-heals the exact crashed-create signature (live worktree at the derived path on exactly `refs/heads/openclaw/<name>`, no registry row) instead of dead-ending: it atomically claims the path in the registry (`insertRegistryWorktreeIfPathFree()`, a single Kysely `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (live row at path)` — no schema change), then re-provisions (`copyIncludedFiles()` + `runSetupScript()`), preserving the caller's `ownerKind`/`ownerId` and recording the real resolved base. Only the claim holder may provision or destroy the path: a losing adopter provably touches nothing, and a holder whose re-provisioning fails removes the worktree and deletes its own row. The registry carries a persisted readiness contract: `readiness ('provisioning'|'ready')` (closed union; additive `ensureColumn` migration per repo precedent — backfill-as-ready is provably safe because no release tag contains the worktrees feature, and unreleased-main builds inserted rows only post-provisioning). The claim inserts `provisioning`; a single UPDATE flips to `ready` only after copy+setup succeed. Every usable-record path is gated on ready (`findLiveByOwner` filters in SQL; the entry shortcut and claim-loser throw a closed `WorktreeProvisioningError`; `restore()` revives as ready; gc reaps provisioning rows older than `PROVISIONING_STALE_MS` — dead holders — restoring background recovery for auto-named orphans, while a reaped-mid-flight create fails closed with `WorktreeProvisioningReapedError`). The gateway protocol's `WorktreeRecordSchema` gains an additive optional `readiness` enum (no version bump). Normal (non-adopting) `create()` uses the identical claim-early ordering (claim immediately after `git worktree add`; both paths share one claim → provision-as-holder → holder-only-cleanup helper), establishing the invariant that an in-flight create always holds a live row — so the no-row+live-worktree signature genuinely means a crashed create, and an in-flight worktree can never be adopted, re-provisioned, or destroyed by a concurrent same-name call. Every new live registry row is uniqueness-enforced through the one claim. `reconcileOrphans()`/gc remains preserve-only (upstream behavior) — background adoption is deliberately not shipped (see Risks). `git.ts` additively parses the porcelain `branch` field for the adoption signature check.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): gc keeps upstream's preserve-only behavior for foreign/detached and live git-listed worktrees (only dead debris and stale provisioning rows are cleaned); no protocol version bump; no changes to snapshot semantics; web UI status label deliberately unchanged (would pull in i18n regeneration disproportionate to this PR).

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker/verifier agents, human-operated); every change was gated on tests written first and independently reviewed by a fresh-context model before submission.

2. Run `service.create({ repoRoot, name: "task-1" })` again.

```

FAIL … adopts a worktree orphaned when create() crashed …, during gc()

FAIL … adopts an orphaned worktree instead of throwing on a retried create() …
```

target.title: fix(agents): lease session worktrees during runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A resumed session's managed git worktree could be deleted out from under an active agent run. Idle GC, a separate remover, or a manual `worktrees.gc` would remove the session's isolated checkout while the run was still using it, destroying in-flight workspace files. The silent counterpart also existed: a session whose managed worktree had already been removed was admitted anyway and ran as if its cwd were an ordinary directory, with no checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a rewrite of the earlier approach after maintainer review. The earlier head used a process-local FIFO lease, which was an exclusive full-run mutex (a parent and a child run sharing one worktree could deadlock), leased only `cwd` (a workspace-only child was unprotected), and leaned on `git worktree lock` as the admission/removal mutex even though that lock is not an atomic cross-process check-and-act.

Runs now take a shared run-lease and removal takes an exclusive claim, both stored as rows in the existing shared-state `state_leases` table. Admission and removal each run inside one `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`, which uses `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`src/infra/sqlite-transaction.ts`), so the read-check-write is serialized across processes by SQLite itself. That single transaction is the atomic admission/removal gate, replacing the git-lock TOCTOU. The git worktree lock is kept only as a secondary raw-Git guard, refcounted per process so a parent and a same-process child do not unlock each other.

Each lease row carries an opaque token plus `pid` and process start time. Run leases and the removal claim are both token-owned: a run releases only its own token, and the removal claim rejects a competing live remover and clears or finalizes only under its own token, so two removers can never enter destructive work on the same worktree at once. Dead or reused-pid owners, including a removal claim whose remover process died before finalizing, are pruned inside the same transaction via `isLockOwnerDefinitelyStale`, so a killed holder never strands the worktree. The worktree id is resolved from the session's stored `worktree.id` binding, or by containment over both the run cwd and workspace dir, so a workspace-only child still leases. Removal claims before any cleanliness or snapshot work and rejects while a live run lease exists.

Choosing the shared state DB over sidecar claim files follows the repository storage policy (SQLite only for runtime registries), and reuses the same cross-process lease table and transaction primitive already used by startup-migration checkpoints.

## User Impact

Users resuming sessions with isolated worktrees can no longer have their live checkout deleted underneath an active run by idle GC, a manual gc, or session cleanup, including when the session works in a subdirectory of the worktree and including when a second process races the removal. A session whose checkout was removed while it was away now fails fast with a clear error instead of silently continuing without its files. Concurrent parent and child runs can share one worktree without deadlocking, and two removers cannot corrupt a worktree by deleting it concurrently.

## Evidence

- Branched off `origin/main` `cba9ffb1`; head `20d188b0`. Mergeable, behind current main.
- Focused suites pass (40 in the worktree group): `src/agents/worktrees/run-lease.test.ts` and `src/agents/worktrees/service.remove-lease.test.ts` cover parent/child shared readers with git-lock refcounting, the workspace-only child id resolution, dead-owner (SIGKILL) pruning, reused-pid (ABA) pruning, force parity, admission-fails-once-removing, dead-remover recovery, exclusive rejection of a second live remover (with and without force), owner-scoped abort that cannot clear a newer claim, a concurrent second remover rejected at the service level, a release that fails on a database error keeping the lease and git guard and then freeing them on retry, and gc skipping a busy worktree; existing `service.test.ts` still passes. `agent.test.ts`, `agent.session.test.ts`, and the gateway worktrees/session-create/session-delete-lifecycle/server-maintenance suites pass unchanged.
- `oxlint --type-aware` and `oxfmt --check` clean on all changed files; `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean.
- Three pre-ship Codex reviews were addressed: a stranded removal marker after a mid-removal crash (fixed by the self-healing pid/start-time owner); an overwritable removal claim whose cleanup was not owner-scoped (fixed by the opaque token, exclusive rejection, and owner-scoped abort); and a lease release that dropped the git guard and became non-retryable when the state-database delete failed (fixed by deleting the row first and dropping the guard only on success, so a failed release retries and the worktree stays protected meanwhile).

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: a resumed session's managed worktree must survive a concurrent separate-process non-force removal while its run is active; a session whose managed worktree was already removed must fail admission instead of running without its checkout; and two removers must not enter destructive removal of the same worktree at once.
Real environment tested: two real OS processes sharing one on-disk git worktree, the real `ManagedWorktreeService` removal path, and the real shared-state SQLite lease store, driven on pristine `origin/main` `597de699` versus this patch `20d188b0` with identical inputs; a genuine second node process holds the run lease while the parent issues the removal, and a second overlapping removal is issued against the real service.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx proof-lease.mts`, which creates a real session-owned git worktree with a nested workspace file, spawns a separate node process that acquires the run lease, issues a non-force `ManagedWorktreeService` removal from the parent while that process holds the lease, releases and re-removes, removes a second worktree and attempts admission for its path, then starts one removal of a third worktree and issues a second overlapping removal against the same service.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine origin/main 597de699)
separate-process run holder: run holds no lease
separate non-force removal during the live run: removed=true
nested session workspace file survived the removal attempt: false
removal after the run ends: rejected: unknown active worktree: 26576991-7aef-4631-90e2-736900df892b
admission for an already-removed managed worktree: no admission guard exists on this tree
second remover racing the first: rejected: git worktree remove failed: fatal: '.../proof-concurrent' is not a working tree
# AFTER (this patch 20d188b0, identical inputs)
separate-process run holder: run holds a lease
separate non-force removal during the live run: rejected: worktree is busy: locked by live pid 3063548
nested session workspace file survived the removal attempt: true
removal after the run ends: removed=true
admission for an already-removed managed worktree: admission fails with: managed worktree was removed: /tmp/openclaw-proof-L9gT62/state/worktrees/b52965bdfb863c5f/proof-removed
second remover racing the first: rejected: worktree removal is already in progress
```
Observed result after fix: while a separate process holds the run lease, a non-force removal is rejected as busy and the run's uncommitted workspace file survives, then succeeds only after the run ends; a second remover racing the first is rejected as already in progress; on the base the same first removal deletes the live checkout and its in-flight file, the second remover instead collides with the first into a corrupt half-removed worktree, and admission for an already-removed worktree proceeds with no guard.
What was not tested: no live provider request, gateway deployment, or multi-host run was exercised; the processes ran on the development Linux host sharing one state directory and git worktree, so cross-process protection rests on the directly exercised SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialization plus the on-disk git worktree lock; the parent/child shared-reader, dead-owner recovery, reused-pid, force-parity, workspace-only, and owner-scoped-abort cases are covered by the regression suite rather than this harness.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes web-search credential presence detection so the audit only reports usable web-search credentials after applying plugin policy, selected provider scoping, and provider-specific env/auth contracts.

The earlier detector could treat credentials from blocked plugins or unrelated providers as web-search credentials. The latest fix also handles the Google plugin's split contracts: selecting `gemini` no longer counts `google-vertex` env such as `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` as a Gemini web-search key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Security/audit surfaces should reflect the selected web-search provider's actual runtime credential contract. Plugin manifests can contain multiple providers and env vars, so manifest env scanning must not flatten unrelated provider credentials into one web-search-positive result.

## User Impact

- Disabled, denied, or non-selected web-search plugins no longer make `web_search` look credentialed.
- Missing env-backed SecretRefs fail closed consistently.
- `tools.web.search.provider: "gemini"` with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` no longer reports Gemini web search as configured.
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` still reports Gemini web search as configured through the selected provider contract.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/web-search-credential-presence.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 26 tests.

- `git diff --check` passed.

## Proof

- Added regression coverage for Google/Gemini-vs-Vertex manifest env scoping: `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` alone is false for selected `gemini`, while `GEMINI_API_KEY` is true.
- Provider-scoped manifest env detection now first reads the selected bundled web-search provider's public contract env vars, then falls back only to same-provider manifest setup/auth env metadata when a public contract is unavailable.
- Existing policy/credential tests still cover plugin allow/deny, disabled entries, keyless providers, raw plugin webSearch credentials, SecretRefs, and explicit provider selection.

target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward the execution abort signal to web search HTTP requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an agent run while a DuckDuckGo `web_search` request is pending leaves that HTTP request running, and the shared provider loop can start another provider after cancellation. The parent execution signal reaches the generic web-search runtime, but the shared fallback loop treats parent abort like an ordinary provider error and continues to the next candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is a two-layer root-cause fix:

1. **Provider layer (DuckDuckGo):** Forward the `AbortSignal` from the tool execution context through the provider to the guarded endpoint helper (`withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`), which already accepts a signal parameter.

2. **Shared runtime layer** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` before each candidate provider attempt and treat `params.signal?.aborted` as terminal in the catch path (`params.signal?.aborted || !allowFallback`). This prevents the shared fallback loop from starting another provider after the user cancels the run — the same canonical fix from SearXNG PR #104216 (zhangguiiping-xydt, 🦞 diamond lobster).

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct Browser `/act` callers sending `clickCoords` could pass hexadecimal coordinate strings such as `"0x10"`, and the route would coerce them into unintended numeric positions instead of rejecting the invalid input.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Browser action route now uses the existing strict route finite-number parser for both `clickCoords.x` and `clickCoords.y`, matching the Browser CLI coordinate contract while preserving decimal coordinate strings such as `"42.5"`. The old permissive route-only numeric helper was removed so this boundary has one canonical parser.

## User Impact

Browser agents and direct Browser control callers get a clear invalid-request response for hex coordinate strings, instead of silently clicking a coerced coordinate.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: Browser `/act` rejects hex string coordinate values for both `clickCoords.x` and `clickCoords.y`, while decimal-string coordinates still perform a real coordinate click through the Browser control server.
- Current head: `acbb44838ae95a9d8fac96f99d5ecfd99c9d83a4`.
- Real Browser behavior proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` started the branch's authenticated loopback Browser bridge with a temporary managed Chromium profile, then drove real HTTP `/start` and `/act` requests. The bearer token and ephemeral ports were redacted from the public transcript.

```json
{
  "head": "acbb44838ae95a9d8fac96f99d5ecfd99c9d83a4",
  "start": { "status": 200, "ok": true },
  "setup": {
    "status": 200,
    "ok": true,
    "result": { "left": 30, "top": 30, "width": 120, "height": 80 }
  },
  "decimalClick": { "status": 200, "ok": true, "url": "about:blank" },
  "clickedReadback": { "status": 200, "ok": true, "result": "1" },
  "hexX": {
    "status": 400,
    "code": "ACT_INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error": "x must be a finite number."
  },
  "hexY": {
    "status": 400,
    "code": "ACT_INVALID_REQUEST",
    "error": "y must be a finite number."
  }
}
```

target.title: refactor(agents): converge CLI tool terminal reason onto run-termination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot and live CLI runners each derived the same terminal decision — `timed_out` / `cancelled` / `failed` for tools when a run ends — with different logic:

- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts` (one-shot) read the abort signal's lifecycle fields, then only recognized `FailoverError` timeouts; a `TimeoutError`-shaped or `AbortError`-shaped run error without an aborted signal classified as `failed`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/claude-live-session.ts` (live) only sniffed error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) and never consulted the abort signal.

Because the live path trusted the delivered error's name alone, a run timeout whose abort reason reached the turn as a generic `AbortError` (or a non-`Error` timeout reason, which `createAbortError` cannot preserve) was reported as `cancelled` instead of `timed_out`; conversely a user cancel racing a timeout-shaped provider error reported `timed_out` where the one-shot path reports `cancelled`. Same decision, two encodings, observable drift — seam 3 of #104219.

## Why This Change Was Made

Converge the derivation onto one owner, per the #104219 change shape. `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` lives in `src/agents/run-termination.ts` — the module that already owns abort→stop-reason semantics (`resolveAgentRunAbortLifecycleFields`) — and encodes one rule: abort-signal lifecycle fields are authoritative when the signal has aborted; error shape (`isTimeoutError`, `FailoverError` timeout, `AbortError` name) classifies otherwise. Both call-site derivations are deleted in the same change; the live turn now carries the run's real abort signal (`ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`, threaded in `createTurn`).

`terminalReason` feeds diagnostic events only (`tool.execution.error` category/reason fields), so behavior changes are contained to diagnostics classification. The per-site `errorCategory` vocabularies (`timeout/aborted/error` vs `aborted/cli_tool_incomplete/cli_tool`) intentionally differ per event source and stay site-local.

## User Impact

Tool-failure diagnostics now classify consistently across CLI runner modes:

- Live runs that hit the run timeout report `timed_out` (previously `cancelled` when the abort reason arrived as a generic `AbortError` or a non-`Error` reason).
- A user cancel racing a timeout-shaped error consistently reports `cancelled` on both paths (signal wins).
- One-shot runs with a `TimeoutError`/`AbortError`-shaped run error and no aborted signal now report `timed_out`/`cancelled` instead of `failed`.

No control-flow, retry, or delivery behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Drift sites and trace: old derivations at `execute.ts` (`resolveToolTerminalReason`) and `claude-live-session.ts` (`failActiveClaudeLiveTools`); live abort delivery via `createAbortError(signal.reason)` loses timeout identity for generic/non-`Error` reasons.
- Tests: table-driven matrix for `resolveCliToolTerminalReason` in `src/agents/run-termination.test.ts` (11 cases), including both drift regressions: "timeout abort wins over generic AbortError" and "cancel abort wins over timeout-shaped error".
- Local: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`, `pnpm check:import-cycles` all exit 0; focused vitest green (`run-termination`, cli-runner suites — 270+ tests).
- Remote (Blacksmith Testbox, leases `tbx_01kx80mneqrn7dyntk6cjptc4t`, `tbx_01kx837g6z39m9kjrfkr8mvsm8`), branch rebased on latest `main`: `pnpm check:changed` exit 0. `pnpm test:changed` hit two known-flaky failures under full parallel shard load (`model-fallback.probe.test.ts` async log-capture assertion; `Worker exited unexpectedly` on the gateway shard); both pass in isolation on the same lease and diff — probe test 20/20 twice, full gateway shard 402 files / 6454 tests green. Neither touches this diff's surface.
- `git diff --numstat`: +43/−17 prod, +96 tests. Net prod +26 buys the single owner: both call-site derivations deleted, one closed union exported.

### Real behavior proof (ephemeral runtime)

Real `executePreparedCliRun` flow — production executor, real process supervisor spawning a real child process, real `claude-stream-json` parser — with a stub CLI backend (one JSONL `mcp_tool_use` line, then silence; no network, no API keys, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`). Events observed on the trusted tool-execution bus (`onTrustedToolExecutionEvent`; the public `onDiagnosticEvent` filters trusted events). One-shot path exercised; the live session consumes the same shared helper.

Timeout run (no-output watchdog → `FailoverError reason:"timeout"`), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-timeout",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-timeout",
  "durationMs": 1509,
  "errorCategory": "cli_tool_incomplete",
  "terminalReason": "timed_out"
}
```

User-cancel run (`abortController.abort()` after `tool.execution.started` → `AbortError` with aborted signal), redacted:

```json
{
  "type": "tool.execution.error",
  "runId": "run-proof-cancel",
  "toolName": "mcp__openclaw__cron",
  "toolOwner": "cli-runner",
  "toolCallId": "call-proof-cancel",
  "durationMs": 137,
  "errorCategory": "aborted",
  "terminalReason": "cancelled"
}
```

**Claude-live path** (same harness family, routed through `shouldUseClaudeLiveSession`: backend id `claude-cli`, `liveSession: "claude-stdio"`; stub waits for the live turn's stdin input, emits a tool use, holds the session; log lines confirm `claude live session start/close reason=abort`). Both events emitted by `failActiveClaudeLiveTools` and carry `toolOwner: "claude-cli"`, exercising the newly threaded `ClaudeLiveTurn.abortSignal`:

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Add native xAI WebSocket streaming TTS through the existing `streamSynthesize` speech-provider contract.

This is separate from xAI realtime voice. It preserves the provider's existing buffered TTS, voice discovery, authentication, and telephony behavior.

## Behavior

- Streams from the canonical `wss://api.x.ai/v1/tts` endpoint.
- Rejects non-canonical streaming bases before bearer-authenticated WebSocket setup, including altered ports, credentials, paths, queries, and fragments.
- Sends ordered `text.delta` frames within xAI's 15,000-character limit, without splitting Unicode surrogate pairs, followed by `text.done`.
- Decodes `audio.delta`, completes on `audio.done`, and propagates server errors.
- Bounds encoded WebSocket frames and cumulative decoded audio.
- Refreshes the idle timeout for every audio chunk.
- Handles close-before-open, cancellation, completion, and repeated `release()` safely.
- Uses existing language, voice, codec, and speed controls; xAI defaults apply to sample rate and bit rate.

The existing Discord caller may deliberately fall back to buffered synthesis when a stream fails. Discord voice requests MP3 through a stream-only xAI provider override, including when a persona is active, while preserving the configured codec for buffered fallback. Other streaming callers retain all five xAI codecs.

## Evidence

Exact head: `a1b159567da31b02eb899b599fbd5584b1a1e598`

```text
Focused provider tests

  extensions/xai/speech-provider.test.ts
  extensions/discord/src/voice/manager.e2e.test.ts

Test typecheck

  policy/import-cycle guards: passed

Official live provider test with a real XAI_API_KEY
  node scripts/test-live.mjs -- extensions/xai/xai.live.test.ts \
    -t "synthesizes TTS through the registered speech provider"
Result: 1 passed, 8 unrelated live cases skipped
The test drained a real stream, asserted output metadata and byte count,
and released the provider stream.

git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
Result: passed

Codex autoreview, gpt-5.5 high
Result: 0 actionable findings; patch is correct (confidence 0.82)
```

An independent current-head review found and eliminated two codec-boundary regressions before publication: restricting valid xAI codecs at the provider boundary, and allowing persona config to override Discord's stream-only MP3 selection. No actionable provider implementation, endpoint, lifecycle, dependency, or lockfile finding remains.

## Dependency

`ws@8.21.0` already existed as an xAI plugin development dependency. This change moves it to runtime dependencies because the production streaming implementation imports it. The dependency guard may therefore require maintainer approval.

## Scope

This PR does not add realtime voice, change buffered TTS behavior, alter Discord's existing fallback decision, expose sample-rate/bit-rate controls, or add a custom xAI proxy. It only makes Discord's streaming request use MP3 while leaving buffered fallback configuration untouched.

No API keys, tokens, credentials, private paths, raw prompts, or raw agent logs are included.

- Rebased and reconstructed the lane in clean worktrees while preserving commits after Windows junction issues affected disposable checkouts.
- Ran focused tests, test typecheck, full repository checks in Crabbox, independent review, Codex autoreview, and finally the official live provider test with a real credential.

### Strongest safe truth

The exact head is test-proven across focused and full repository checks and runtime-proven for registered-provider native xAI streaming TTS. It is not claimed as a live Discord end-to-end proof, and it does not change Discord's pre-existing buffered fallback policy.

target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

target.title: feat(write): add append mode to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The write tool always overwrites files. An `append: true` parameter lets the agent add content to the end of an existing file instead of replacing it. The agent requested this capability repeatedly in real sessions — it wants to write logs, build up checklists incrementally, and extend existing scripts without re-reading them first.

## Why This Change Was Made

Write-tool silent data loss (#40001) can happen when an agent writes to a file it has already edited without re-reading the current content. An append mode gives the agent a safer option: it can add new content without risking the loss of previous edits.

## What Changed

- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to the schema, `WriteOperations.appendFile` method, append branch in `execute`, append-aware recovery (`isRecoveredAppendContent`), and post-mutation abort check matching `edit.ts:460-463`.
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-contracts.ts` — add `append?: boolean` to `WriteToolInput`.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts` — wire `appendFile` for host (`fs.appendFile`), workspace (`root.append()`), and sandbox (read-modify-write, since the sandbox bridge has no native append).
- `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.test.ts` — 7 new tests covering: basic append, append-to-new-file, no-op short-circuit for overwrite, malformed append param rejection, append-identical-content preserving duplicates, append-after-abort recovery via readback, and abort-surfaced-when-append-did-not-persist.

## User Impact

- `append: true` is opt-in. The default write behavior is unchanged.
- Append to a non-existent file creates it (matching `>>` shell semantics).
- The write tool description and prompt snippet advertise the new parameter.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
